thread:
maria-ops: Heads up — saw a viewer in the Console claiming Edit access when using the new role matrix refactor. Repro steps: open project X -> Inspect policy -> UI shows "Edit" button but API returns 403 on save. :confused:

daniel-sec: Ugh. Which project? Can you paste the policy blob? suspect mapping between console perms and enforcement layer got out of sync during the recent role split.

maria-ops: Project `redwood-payments` (prod-ish). Policy snippet from the console UI inspector:

```
roles: ["viewer","editor_v2"]
ui_permissions: { can_edit: true }
enforced_permissions: ["project.read"]
```

maria-ops: The UI shows can_edit true, but the enforcement layer only has project.write missing. Audit logs show 403 on `PATCH /projects/:id` from web-client.

ryan-sre: Interesting. We added the `editor_v2` label but forgot to populate the `enforced_permissions` mapping in the migration job. Migration created the new RBAC rows but the UI mapping reads `ui_permissions` from the role template table. So inconsistency between two tables.

ashley-devex: That explains why some folks saw edit controls but couldn't save. UX is intentionally optimistic (render based on role label). We should gate UI on enforcement API until we finish backfilling. Quick fix: hide edit controls unless enforcement API returns has_permission=true.

elaine-product: We need minimal product impact — hiding edit buttons for everyone could break workflows. Can we scope gating to project role types that went through the refactor (how to detect?)

daniel-sec: There are two actionable items: (1) emergency backfill to populate enforcement permissions for any role with `*_v2` suffix, (2) UI gating change to use enforcement check for write actions only. Backfill should be safe but we must log extensive audit events. Also check KMS audit for any key-related anomalies (we saw an odd KMS audit entry around the same time in prod).

maria-ops: I spotted a KMS log with key_id = null for a call from `console-service` at 02:14 UTC — looks like it failed to decrypt a small payload before the 403s. Could be unrelated but worth triage.

ryan-sre: Can you paste the KMS log id? we should check if the console attempted to fetch a per-project secret while the role mapping was inconsistent (secret access requires project.write).

maria-ops: klog-20250312-021413-7f9a


daniel-sec: I'll pull the KMS logs. If console-service called KMS and key_id is null that usually means our key fetcher returned nil because the project lookup failed — fits the hypothesis (UI rendered edit button, backend rejected, backend didn't fetch key). No obvious cryptographic issue from first glance.

ashley-devex: Proposed immediate steps:
- api: run backfill job for `*_v2` roles (low risk) :gear:
- ui: gate edit controls on enforcement API (quick patch) :hammer_and_wrench:
- observability: add a dashboard for mismatches between ui_permissions and enforced_permissions :bar_chart:
- audit: log a migration_event for every changed role and KMS access attempt IDs into the audit index :ledger:

elaine-product: Timeline? we should notify support and customer success for affected projects before toggling UI behavior.

ryan-sre: I can run the backfill now in dry-run to see counts. If counts < 200 projects, we can do live backfill with low blast radius. I'll scope it to orgs with recent activity first.

daniel-sec: Also add a short-term policy check to the enforcement layer: if UI shows can_edit but enforcement denies, return header `X-Perm-Inconsistent: true` so UI can log telemetry. Helps correlate incidents.

maria-ops: Adding that header will make it easier to find broken sessions. I'll open a small ticket for support template messaging.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: `rbac-backfill-dryrun` -> staging at 1748123500, prod canary at 1748127200 if approved.

ashley-devex: I'll prepare the UI patch and a feature flag `ui.enforce_write_checks`. If dry-run counts look reasonable, flip the flag for affected orgs only.

daniel-sec: One more security note: when we backfill, ensure we don't accidentally escalate any role. Backfill must be conservative (derive enforced_permissions as intersection of current enforcement policy and role template defaults). No auto-add of write perms unless explicit mapping exists.

elaine-product: Good. Can someone post the exact criteria for detection (how to flag roles as migrated_v2) so support can search customers?

ryan-sre: Detection criteria: role template name endswith `_v2` OR role_matrix.version >= 2 AND ui_permissions.can_edit == true AND enforced_permissions does not include `project.write`. I'll add query in the incident doc.

maria-ops: Thanks team — running the initial queries and will attach counts here in a follow-up message. :thumbsup:
